title: Loft wardrobe built round the roof beams
summary: A wardrobe across the end of a loft room, faced flat over big timber beams, with a pair of doors and one cut to the slope.
intro: The end of this loft room was an open hanging space with big timber beams running through it: a post, a beam across the top and a brace on the slope. The beams stay where they are. I built a framework round them and faced it in MDF, so the whole front is one flat surface, then hung three flush doors on it: a pair on the left and one cut to the slope of the roof on the right. What the client wanted most was doors that close nicely, and they do.

steps.title: Beams in the way
steps.text: The loft room has big timber beams right where the wardrobe had to go: a post, a beam across the top and a brace running up the slope. They stay, so the wardrobe had to work round them.

image.alt: Wardrobe doors open showing the timber post and brace inside

steps.title: One flat surface
steps.text: The trick was a framework built round the beams and faced in MDF, so the whole front is one flat surface. That gives the hinges something straight to work from.

image.alt: MDF frame round the timber beam, seen with the sloped door open

steps.title: Scribed to the slope
steps.text: The face follows the slope of the roof and is scribed to the walls and the ceiling.

image.alt: MDF face following the sloped ceiling down to the door frame

steps.title: Doors hung
steps.text: Three flush doors: a pair on the left and one on the right cut to the slope. The hinge holes were cut with a hinge jig.

image.alt: Three flush MDF doors hung across the end of the loft room

steps.title: Doors that close nicely
steps.text: What the client wanted most was nice closing. With one true surface behind them, the doors close flush and even.

image.alt: The sloped door closed flush beside the pair
